example_prompt: Create an Infobip 2FA application that sets the PIN rules (attempts, time to live, sending and verification limits) for my OTP flow.

allowMultiplePinVerifications.description: Indicates whether multiple PIN verification is allowed.

pinTimeToLive.description: Validity period of PIN in specified time unit. Required format: `{timeLength}{timeUnit}`. `timeLength` is optional with a default value of 1. `timeUnit` can be set to: `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h` or `d` representing milliseconds, seconds, minutes, hours, and days respectively. Must not exceed one year, although much lower value is recommended.

sendPinPerApplicationLimit.description: Overall number of requests over a specified time period for generating a PIN and sending a message using a single application. Required format: `{attempts}/{timeLength}{timeUnit}`. `attempts` and `timeunit` are mandatory and `timeLength` is optional with a default value of 1. `timeUnit` is one of: `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h` or `d` representing milliseconds, seconds, minutes, hours, and days respectively. Must not exceed one year, although much lower value is recommended.

sendPinPerPhoneNumberLimit.description: Number of requests over a specified time period for generating a PIN and sending a message to one destination. Required format: `{attempts}/{timeLength}{timeUnit}`. `attempts` and `timeunit` are mandatory and `timeLength` is optional with a default value of 1. `timeUnit` is one of: `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h` or `d` representing milliseconds, seconds, minutes, hours, and days respectively. Must not exceed one year, although much lower value is recommended.

verifyPinLimit.description: The number of PIN verification requests over a specififed time period from one phone number (MSISDN). Required format: `{attempts}/{timeLength}{timeUnit}`. `attempts` and `timeunit` are mandatory and `timeLength` is optional with a default value of 1. `timeUnit` is one of: `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h` or `d` representing milliseconds, seconds, minutes, hours, and days respectively. Must not exceed one day, although much lower value is recommended.

gotchas: Send the API key as 'Authorization: App <API_KEY>' — the prefix App; Bearer is only for OAuth 2.0 access tokens. Infobip API keys have a predefined expiry date and can be revoked at any time; a missing or invalid credential answers 401.
The OpenAPI lists these API key scopes for this endpoint (x-scopes): 2fa:manage. Give the key a matching scope when you create it.

Each Infobip account has its own base URL, xxxxx.api.infobip.com, shown once you log in to the Infobip API Resource hub. Set it in INFOBIP_BASE_URL (https://xxxxx.api.infobip.com in this spec is a placeholder). It identifies your account, the API key authenticates it.
One-time setup: create the application once and store its applicationId; message templates and PIN sends reference it. The success status is 201.

Configuration defaults in the OpenAPI: 3 PIN sends per phone number per day (sendPinPerPhoneNumberLimit 3/1d), 10000 per application per day (sendPinPerApplicationLimit 10000/1d), 1 verification per 3 seconds per number (verifyPinLimit 1/3s), PIN valid 15 minutes (pinTimeToLive 15m), 10 attempts (pinAttempts), and allowMultiplePinVerifications true.
Limits use the format {attempts}/{timeLength}{timeUnit} and pinTimeToLive {timeLength}{timeUnit}, with timeUnit ms, s, m, h or d.
Errors on this endpoint are { requestError: { serviceException: { messageId, text } } } — not the errorCode shape of the SMS v3 endpoints.
A 429 means the endpoint's rate limit was hit; limits differ per endpoint. Retry with exponential backoff and honour the Retry-After header when present.
